status_summary: Executive orders place several of the chapter's topics under the Domestic Policy Council (DPC) or its head: the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy convenes DEI-tracking meetings (EO 14151, 2025-01-20) and receives agency compliance reports on DEI in federal contracting (EO 14398, 2026-03-26); the White House Faith Office sits within the DPC (EO 14205, 2025-02-07); the Religious Liberty Commission advises the Faith Office and the DPC (EO 14291, 2025-05-01); and the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy is executive director of the Make America Healthy Again Commission, which the HHS Secretary chairs (EO 14212, 2025-02-13). On immigration, Reuters reported on 2025-07-11 that Stephen Miller, the deputy chief of staff for policy, leads the White House Homeland Security Council, which coordinates immigration and other domestic security policy across the administration, and that his group was unaffected by the National Security Council (NSC) downsizing; NSPM-1 (2025-01-20) lets the NSC convene as the Homeland Security Council on pre-agreed topics with one staff. Other topics run outside the councils: energy went to a new National Energy Dominance Council chaired by the Interior Secretary (EO 14213, 2025-02-14), while EO 14154 (2025-01-20) names the National Economic Council director only as a consulted official, and the Homeland Security Task Forces in EO 14159 are set up by the Attorney General and the Homeland Security Secretary. The NSC staff was cut sharply in May 2025 with the Secretary of State as interim national security adviser, and a July-August 2026 Foreign Service Journal commentary says policy advice runs largely through informal channels rather than the interagency process. No published allocation of overlapping topics (immigration, health, energy, trade) to a single council was found. EO 14291 set the Religious Liberty Commission to end on 2026-07-04 unless the President extended it; a Justice Department notice published 2026-08-07 (91 FR 51180) announced the Commission's eighth meeting for 2026-08-17 to finalize its report, without citing an extension. Inference: the objective is partly met in the DPC-led and Homeland Security Council-led areas and is not documented as a formal tiered-committee design elsewhere.

timeline.event: NSPM-1 reorganizes the NSC system: the NSC may convene as the Homeland Security Council on topics agreed in advance by the national security and homeland security advisors, one staff and one Executive Secretary serve both, and NSC staff chair policy coordination committees.
EO 14151 assigns the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy to convene monthly meetings with OMB, OPM and deputy agency heads to track the end of DEI programs.

EO 14154 (Unleashing American Energy) directs OMB, CEQ and agencies on energy and permitting and consults the National Economic Council director on agency action plans; it does not name the Domestic Policy Council or a National Energy Dominance Council.

EO 14205 establishes the White House Faith Office within the Domestic Policy Council, which makes recommendations to the President through the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy (published 2025-02-12).

EO 14212 (published 2025-02-19) creates the Make America Healthy Again Commission, chaired by the HHS Secretary, with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy as executive director and the National Economic Council director and the Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy among the members.

EO 14213 (published 2025-02-20) creates the National Energy Dominance Council in the Executive Office of the President, chaired by the Interior Secretary, with the economic, domestic and national security assistants as members; a cabinet-led body rather than an NEC- or DPC-led process.

EO 14291 (published 2025-05-07) establishes the Religious Liberty Commission, which advises the White House Faith Office and the Domestic Policy Council; the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy is an ex officio member and the Justice Department provides its support.

The National Security Council is sharply reduced, with some staff placed on leave and Secretary of State Marco Rubio serving as interim head after Michael Waltz is moved aside (reported 2025-05-24); aides are quoted as saying policy decisions are largely made by the President.

Reuters reports that Stephen Miller, deputy chief of staff for policy, leads the White House Homeland Security Council, which coordinates immigration and other domestic security policy across the administration; his homeland group was unaffected by the NSC downsizing, and most internal details come from anonymous current or former officials.

EO 14398 (published 2026-03-31) on DEI in federal contracting has agency heads report compliance to the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and has OMB identify at-risk sectors in coordination with that official.

The American Foreign Service Association's Foreign Service Journal (July-August 2026 issue, month-level date) carries a critical commentary saying the NSC's formal structure has been sidelined and that advice runs largely through informal channels, which it says has stifled coordination.

title: Have White House policy councils lead cross-cutting priority processes
uncertainties: Most evidence is documentary (which official receives which report or chairs which body) and does not show how the councils run their committees day to day. EO 14159's task-force section names the Attorney General and the Homeland Security Secretary and no council (read in the earlier pass, not reopened). Stephen Miller's leadership of the Homeland Security Council rests on a Reuters report of 2025-07-11 that relies largely on anonymous officials, and on an NPR report of the November 2024 announcement; NSPM-1 names no officeholders, and the earlier law-firm alert (Akin Gump, undated) was not reopened. The Foreign Service Journal item is a critical commentary from a Foreign Service association, an attributed characterization, and its page excerpt gives no dates or staffing numbers. A trade-policy report found by search (Bessent, Lutnick and Greer leading negotiations) carried no publication date and was not used. No 2026 report on council jurisdiction changes was found. Searches run: Stephen Miller roles; NSC shrunk under Rubio and interagency process; who runs trade policy; Miller and the Homeland Security Council process. EO 14291 sets a 2026-07-04 end date for the Religious Liberty Commission unless extended; a Federal Register meeting notice of 2026-08-07 shows the Commission still meeting, but no extension order was found or read.
